caveats: The API is queried every Wednesday. If new data is available, the dataset is automatically updated.
methodology_other: Vessel Count uses real-time data on vessel movements—Automatic Identification System (AIS) signals of vessels— to calculate the yearly average number of ships passing through the chokepoint, over the timeframe 2019-2024. These yearly averages are available by 5 main ship categories (container, dry bulk, general cargo, ro-ro and tanker) plus the total. https://www.imf.org/en/publications/wp/issues/2021/08/20/tracking-trade-from-space-an-application-to-pacific-island-countries-464345
name: ports
notes: The PortWatch ports database includes 1,854 ports globally along with other [associated information](https://portwatch.imf.org/datasets/acc668d199d1472abaaf2467133d4ca4/about). This dataset shows the satellite-based vessel data from the UN Global Platform, this monitor provides real-time indicators of port and shipment activity for the ports.

organization.title: PortWatch
organization.description:
PortWatch offers cutting edge analytical tools to help users assess the domestic and international trade impact of actual and future disasters, such as extreme weather events. Building on extensive research, PortWatch uses satellite-based vessel data and big data analytics to produce actionable insights for policymakers, international organizations and the general public.

PortWatch is a joint initiative of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the University of Oxford, and Delft University of Technology.
